Date: 2027-10-01T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Request: non-learning attestation + operational evidence for pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — OptiHealth is excited to kick off the pilot. Before we move forward our legal & security teams want a short attestation + a pragmatic evidence package proving that our tenant data will not be used to improve models (no-training / no-learn). Specifically they asked for:

- A signed attestation we can attach to our procurement packet.
- A short ops checklist describing how you isolate tenant data (KV cache, ephemeral logs).
- Sample logs or a sanitized transfer showing how export/on-demand deletion works (we only need a small sample).
- Confirmation of which subprocessors will see prompt/response artifacts and any cross-border flows.
- KMS / key custody options for on-prem or customer-managed keys.

Can you point us to the minimal set of artifacts we can expect within 5 business days? If some items require more time, please flag which will take longer and why.

Sonal
Sonal Mehta
Head of Customer Ops, OptiHealth
sonal.mehta@optihealth.com

Note: Legal is aware of the pilot SOW but wants these items documented before signature.

High-level timeline (target):
1) Within 3 business days: draft attestation PDF + ops checklist + list of subprocessors and flows.
2) Within 5 business days: sanitized sample export (SFTP/CSV) and short note on audit logs retention windows.
3) If you require on-prem evidence or HSM screenshots, that will take ~10 business days to gather and validate with infra.

Open questions for your team so we scope the artifacts correctly:
- Do you need the attestation notarized or is an e-signed company officer signature sufficient?
- For sample logs, do you prefer API-export (JSON) or SFTP-delivered CSV?
- Any residency constraints (must remain in US-only)?

We'll attach the standard redwood-non-learning-attestation and an ops checklist draft in the next message.

Thanks — Marissa

Hi Sonal — thanks, and good clarifications. Attached is the signed attestation (executive signature), the ops-checklist CSV, and a sanitized sample export delivered via SFTP stubbed file. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

- E-sign: acceptable. I've attached an attestation signed by our VP of Product (dated 2027-10-04).
- Sample export: we created an SFTP drop with a single sanitized CSV row and a readme describing redaction rules (attached sftp-transfer-sample.txt).
- Subprocessors: current subprocessors that may touch transient prompt/response artifacts are listed in the subprocessors section of the attestation. All subprocessors we use for inference routing and telemetry are contractually bound by our no-learning controls for accounts that opt into no-train. We'll include a short legal sentence in the attestation to that effect.
- Fallback behavior: routing policies preserve non-learning flag — if a request is routed to a compatible model variant in another capacity tier, we continue to honor the no-train setting. Exceptions (e.g., emergency debug where data must be captured) require explicit, documented customer consent and are treated as an opt-in debug session; we will not capture those artifacts for model improvement unless you explicitly allow it.

Next steps:
1) Confirm that the attached attestation format is acceptable for procurement (signer title + date).
2) If yes, we'll send the final signed PDF and SFTP credentials for the sample.
3) Connor will follow up with a short ops-runbook for your CS/DevOps to validate deletion/exports (target by EOD Mon).

Attachments in this thread: redwood-non-learning-attestation.pdf (signed), ops-checklist-no-learn.csv, sftp-transfer-sample.txt

Thanks — Marissa
